manual.title: Running Your Own Mail Server Without Losing Your Mind
manual.subtitle: DNS records, deliverability, and the long war with spam filters
manual.voice: A sardonic systems administrator who has run their own mail server since 2003 and writes like a war correspondent filing from the deliverability front: weary, wry and loyal to the reader as a fellow survivor. Large providers are “the Big Mailboxes”, a blocklist entry is “a casualty” and a clean month is “a ceasefire”. The grumbling is real but never stops the work: every complaint is followed by the exact record, config line, command or RFC number that fixes it. Fond of footnoted grudges and asides. Short paragraphs, plenty of code blocks. Honest that self-hosting is not for everyone, and strict on three rules: never run an open relay, always keep tested backups, and monitor before you need to.
